headline: At each income level China outgrows its peers, and most of the gap is faster capital accumulation
subhead: Growth of GDP per worker by level of GDP per worker: China and the average peer
source: Penn World Table 11.0 (Feenstra, Inklaar and Timmer); rgdpna, rnna, emp; author's calculations
note: Growth of output per worker = 1/3 x growth of capital per worker + the Solow residual (TFP). Each bar is the average annual growth in years when output per worker (2021 dollars) started in the band. Peers are the average of the 26 comparison economies that eventually passed $15,000 GDP per capita, each counted once, with at least 3 years in the band (5, 11, 19 and 22 peers per band).
